non_blocking.what: Two validations from design sec 12 are not enforced. waitedMs has no 8-hour ceiling (`--waited-ms 99999999999` exits 0; the value only goes into the rules.check event) and CheckOptions.caller is not checked at run time. On the command line, `--signal __proto__=true` is silently dropped (assigning to __proto__ on a plain object does nothing, Object.hasOwn then misses it) and exits 0 instead of the usage error that any other unknown name gets. No verdict or file is affected. Fix: reject waitedMs above 28_800_000 and a caller outside cli/library in checkOptions, and build the --signal object with Object.create(null) or a Map.

When the caller gives glm-peak=true without --peak-until, the end of the peak is never taken from a live heartbeat's nextChangeAt, although the design's CheckOptions.peakUntil comment says it is read from the heartbeat when not given, and ORCHESTRATION 16.10 says 'no peakUntil: take the heartbeat's nextChangeAt'. The code only uses nextChangeAt when the glm-peak value itself came from the heartbeat. The code's choice avoids mixing a caller value with a host's change time, but the doc sentence is broader than the behaviour. Align one of them.

The condition phrase for a signal omits the source parenthetical the design sec 6.4 sample shows ('code-freeze is on (set by the human at 14:02)'). Shared with the gate, so FEAT-006 should add it when it wires the gate; no gate exists yet to disagree with.

A queue text without a ticket differs from the gate's in three places, not the two the FEAT step names (the third drops '/rules let q-N', which would name a ticket that does not exist). Deliberate, listed as interpretation 2 and in ORCHESTRATION 16.10, pinned by the spec. Recorded only so FEAT-006's gate-versus-checkCall text test uses the same three substitutions.
